author: Mitch Anderson
title: REVEALED: Oil Sands Alliance is Lobbying Mark Carney’s Government Almost Daily
content:
Prime Minister Mark Carney’s once-impressive reputation as a global climate leader has fallen fast. A United Nations 

Special Envoy

 on Climate Action and Finance as recently as January 2025, Carney was just named by 

Newsweek

 as number two on its list of the top 50 climate heretics, ahead of climate change denier U.S. President Donald Trump.  




One cohort, however, must be very pleased with Carney’s performance. The 

Oil Sands Alliance

 and its members have lobbied the federal government 588 times since Carney came into office, according to a DeSmog analysis.




The Oil Sands Alliance (OSA) has been steadily increasing its lobbying over time, reaching an average of 6.7 times per week under Mark Carney’s government. 




The OSA (formerly known as the Pathways Alliance) was formed in 2022 by Canada’s largest bitumen companies including Canadian Natural Resources, Suncor, Imperial Oil, Cenovus and ConocoPhillips, representing 95 percent of oil sands production. The individual companies have been lobbying the federal government individually for decades, and now have another avenue to do so through OSA. Its original stated goal was to bring oil sands emissions to net zero by 2050, a high profile talking point conspicuously abandoned after changes to the federal 

Competition Act

 in 2024.

author: Edward Donnelly
title: Carbon Capture Delusion Returns to Haunt COP31
content:
Last year, if the fossil fuel industry had been running its combined deployment of carbon capture and storage (CCS) projects at full throttle, it would only have soaked up 0.17 percent — a tiny fraction of a fraction — of the world’s carbon dioxide emissions. In reality, the actual figure was even smaller, probably just over half that amount, according to a new report by 

researchers

 at Imperial College London, since many carbon capture projects don’t operate close to their stated capacity.




Not a stunningly impressive performance for a technique first deployed more than half a century ago. What is arguably more stunning is that the 

draft

 

text

In other words, the framers of this text are trying to sell the world on the idea that the fossil fuel industry can expand global CCS capacity by anywhere from 19 to 37 times current levels of 68 million tonnes in less than a decade — and will likely need an even greater increase to meet 2035 capture targets if many projects continue to operate below par.

content:

author: Clare Carlile and Hazel Healy
title: Fertiliser, Big Meat and Biofuels Industry Among 260 Food Sector Lobbyists at COP31
content:
Polluting food and agriculture companies are present in large numbers at this year’s UN COP31 climate talks, with a total of 260 lobbyists on the ground in Turkey’s southern city of Antalya, new analysis shows.




The meat and dairy sector, which 

produces

 over 14 percent of global emissions, brought 71 delegates, the highest number of all food and agriculture sectors. Its representatives outnumber delegates from Honduras, where millions of people currently 

face

 severe drought. 




Fertiliser lobbyists showed the biggest jump in delegates year on year, with a 45 percent increase. The CEOs of several powerful trade groups representing the meat, fertiliser, pesticides and biofuels sectors are also present in Antalya. 




Some of the world’s largest agribusiness firms, including meat company 

JBS

 and dairy multinationals 

Nestlé

 and Danone, as well as pesticides firm 

Bayer

 and food giant Unilever, also travelled to Turkey for the talks, which run from 9-20 November.




The analysis shows the power and influence enjoyed by the sector, with more than a hundred lobbyists participating as part of their country governments, lending them privileged access to negotiations. More than 44 percent of food and agriculture delegates travelled on country badges, up from 5 percent at COP27 five years ago.

author: Rebecca John
title: Big Oil, Climate Change, and a ‘Smoking Gun’
content:
Arnold Obguia did not leave the island. According to the forecast, it was no big deal, just another tropical storm. But a few hours later, the winds escalated rapidly, bringing waves so large they almost pulled him out to sea. Clinging to a piece of broken sea wall, Arnold survived to find his house completely destroyed. Others were not so lucky.






















 
















This story is published in partnership with 

Rolling Stone.













Typhoon Rai, known locally as Typhoon Odette, battered the Philippines in December 2021. With winds of up to 167 miles per hour, extreme rainfall, violent storm surges, extensive flooding, and landslides across the central Philippine archipelago, Odette ripped rooftops from houses and devastated crops, engulfing people and property in torrents of fast-flowing floodwater. A Category 5 cyclone, Odette displaced nearly 

3.2 million people

, killing 400, injuring over 1,000, and causing nearly a billion US dollars in damages.




Now, Arnold and other victims of the typhoon are demanding their day in court, filing a civil 

lawsuit

oil and gas giant Shell

title: How a Republican Conservation Group Became a Data Center Booster
content:

The American Conservation Coalition (ACC)

An investigation by DeSmog has found that in the past year the ACC, which runs chapters across college campuses and has roughly 150,000 members, has come out in favor of data centers and has pushed messaging that they are a strategic neccesity.




It’s partnered with AI and gas companies to influence stakeholders. author: Taylor Noakes
title: ‘Grassroots’ Pro-Industry Group Receives Millions in Sponsorship Money, Financial Records Show
content:
One of Canada’s loudest fossil fuel advocacy groups, 

Canada Action

, has for years claimed to be a “grassroots” organization funded through donations from ordinary Canadians.




But financial records obtained by DeSmog reveal that individual donations only make up a tiny percentage of the group’s funding, representing just 0.5 percent of Canada Action’s total revenue for 2024.




The vast majority of its funding instead comes from “sponsorships”, which in the past 

has included contributions

 from Cenovus, the country’s third-largest oil and gas producer. Canada Action previously received $100,000 from the oil and gas company 

ARC Resources

.




Records show that Canada Action received over $2.9 million from sponsorships in 2024, compared to just $15,604 in donations.




The gap between its donations and sponsorship revenue suggests that the non-profit group is mainly being supported by large businesses as opposed to a movement of working Canadians, according to Shane Gunster, a professor at Simon Fraser University’s School of Communications.




“It is a classic example of a ‘subsidized public’ PR strategy in which corporations identify individuals and groups who are sympathetic to their aims, and then ‘subsidize’ their participation within social media networks and the public sphere,” said Gunster in a statement to DeSmog. “The industry or corporation thereby appea

author: Oscar Rothstein
title: Somalia’s Parliament and Public Are Questioning the President’s Shadowy Oil Deal With Turkey
content:
In 2011, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan made a bold move. At a time when no non-African leader had visited Mogadishu in nearly two decades, he took the trip to the conflict-torn capital of Somalia.




Battered by al Shabaab rebels and severe drought, Somalia was in the midst of widespread famine and displacement. During his visit to Mogadishu, Erdoğan called for greater global attention to the country’s plight and promised extensive humanitarian funding to address the crisis.




Fifteen years later, what began as humanitarian cooperation has sprawled into an ever-closer strategic partnership spanning fisheries, space technology, education, healthcare, aviation, regional diplomacy, security, trade, infrastructure — and oil. 




According to documents obtained by Nordic Monitor, an investigative media outlet run by exiled Turkish journalists, a recent agreement between the two nations has given the Turkish Petroleum Corporation (TPAO), Turkey’s state-owned oil company, exclusive drilling rights in three large offshore blocks of gas and oil off the coast of Somalia along with extraordinary financial concessions. The deal is being met with heavy scepticism by Somali MPs, who question whether it really benefits the country, and driving a rise in anti-Turkish sentiment among the public.

title: UN Fails to Disclose Company Names on Biodiversity Summit Delegates List
content:
Hundreds of representatives from the world’s most powerful industry bodies representing sectors that harm, or exploit, the natural world were present on the ground at the October nature summit in Armenia, DeSmog can reveal.




This year, the UN’s Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) moved to reduce public scrutiny over corporate presence, stripping company affiliations from the 9,300-strong delegates list. 




The move came amid 

calls

 for reform of multilateral summits, which have come under fire for granting 

too much power

 to obstructive polluter interests. 




In-depth analysis of the COP17 delegates list shows the official number of business  attendees stood at nearly 480 – a 60 percent drop 

compared

 to COP16, the previous biannual CBD summit, in the context of a 30 percent drop in overall attendance.




But specific sectors, with a strong commercial interest in biodiversity negotiations, sent large delegations to COP17, the analysis shows. Big pharma brought 16 delegates, the same number as the pesticide and agricultural technology sector. The mining industry brought 14, while the finance industry had 128 delegates at the talks, which aimed to mobilise global action to reverse the drastic global decline in plant and animal life.

author: TJ Jordan and Cécile Marchand
title: How a French Oil Executive Is Working With the Trump Administration to ‘Kill’ Europe’s Methane Plan
content:
A TotalEnergies executive is working with U.S. officials to delay the implementation of new European Union methane rules, raising questions over the company’s pledges to tackle leaks of the potent greenhouse gas.




François-Régis Mouton, formerly vice-president of gas advocacy at TotalEnergies, has been representing the International Association of Oil and Gas Producers (IOGP), a London-based fossil fuel lobby group, on an assignment from the French oil giant since 2018.




Mouton has repeatedly shared and engaged with hard right, anti-renewable energy and climate science-denial content on his personal social media, a review by DeSmog and French environmental newsroom Vert found.




Mouton, who serves as IOGP’s Europe managing director, met with U.S. federal officials on at least three occasions to discuss the European Union Methane Regulation (EUMR) in the past 14 months, according to social media posts. The new framework would force oil and gas importers to meet certain standards for methane leaks in their supply chains or face big fines.

Vert

content:

That is the pitch that Canada’s leading AI company, Cohere, is making to the oil and gas industry, even as its CEO Aidan Gomez argues publicly that it is important for the tech industry to be aligned with “environmental goals.”




“As energy demand surges globally, driven in part by the explosive growth of AI data centers, oil and gas companies face significantly new operational, market, and environmental pressures,” explains a 

Cohere e-book

An 

X post

title: Revealed: Pro-AI Data Center Group Spending At Least $2.54M on TV Ads to Influence Ohio Election
content:
A pro-AI data center group purchased at least $2.54 million worth of television ads that ran recently in Ohio, a new DeSmog analysis reveals. The group, Build American AI, is linked to Leading the Future, a major AI industry super PAC backed by Silicon Valley billionaires.

Vance’s term, and former three-term Democratic Senator Sherrod Brown.




“When some people hear data centers they picture computers and servers,” says one Build American AI ad. “But we see something different: electricians, engineers, manufacturers.” The ad states that data centers have brought more than $40 billion in investments and created over 95,000 jobs in Ohio.




“The future won’t be built by politicians or special interests,” 

states

The ads appeared on at least 16 Ohio television stations between September 7 and October 21, according to Build American AI’s 

filings

title: Ohio Denies Evidence of Fracking Waste in Drinking Water. Its Own Records Show Otherwise.
content:
This story was co-published with Rolling Stone.




In Ohio’s rural southeastern corner, Marietta College geology professor David Jeffrey was among the residents worried that industry activity in America’s booming natural gas region could be polluting their drinking water. That’s “the biggest fear,” he said at an August meeting with top Ohio officials.




When Jeffrey and residents from advocacy groups Buckeye Environmental Network and Washington County for Safe Drinking Water met with Ohio officials, those state officials repeatedly assured residents that despite the up to 1.4 billion gallons of oil and gas wastewater injected in underground wells in their county and across Ohio each year, the state was unaware of any resulting drinking water contamination there.




“We would have heard about it,” Mary Mertz, director of the Ohio Department of Natural Resources (ODNR), which oversees both aspects of Ohio’s environment and its oil and gas industry, told residents in the August 17 virtual meeting.




“No one has called us that I’m aware of,” said Eric Vendel, ODNR’s oil and gas division chief. “We have a water investigation form that can be filled out and we would have my team down there and investigate the water.”

title: President Trump Unveils EPA’s New Contradictory Methane Proposal at Campaign Rally
content:
At a Tuesday campaign rally for Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton in Lubbock, Texas, President Trump announced the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) proposal to roll back a Biden-era methane rule, setting up a likely future showdown in how the agency oversees climate pollution under the Clean Air Act.




The proposal marks a break from the agency’s previous approaches to greenhouse gas regulation by maintaining that — for now — the EPA still has the authority to regulate climate pollution from the oil and gas industry, though it might revisit this decision later. With affordability top of mind for many midterm voters, however, the President framed the move in economic terms.   




“Tonight I’m officially terminating Biden’s expensive and unnecessary methane regulations,” Trump announced to the crowd, located near the oil-rich Permian Basin. The new plan would loosen federal requirements for oil and gas operators to detect and repair leaks, ease restrictions on gas flaring, and eliminate the Super Emitter Program, a third-party monitoring and reporting system designed to identify major releases of methane, known as a

author: Mary Stuart
title: How the Far-Right Uses Climate Disasters to Build Political Power
content:
Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor’s 

End Times Fascism and the Fight for the Living World

 is critical reading for anyone seeking to understand and push back against the far-right coalitions wielding considerable state and corporate power around the world.




Klein and Taylor posit that today’s fascists believe that end times have arrived, and have made it their mission to profit from cascading global crises, while hunkering down and protecting themselves as the world burns around them.




The book details three factions of end times fascists, united by their shared apocalypticism. The religious fundamentalists believe end times are upon us, but they will be saved by their messiah. The Silicon Valley technologists are building technologies they say could be world-ending, that in the meantime are killing jobs, consuming vast resources, and polluting communities. The ethno-nationalists espouse conspiratorial ideas about cultural replacement and treat immigration as an existential threat.




DeSmog Canada editor/reporter Mary Stuart spoke with Astra Taylor about how climate change fits into end times fascism, the importance of AI data centre fights, and how we can understand Canadian Prime Minister Carney’s neoliberal moves in response to U.S. President Donald Trump.

title: Interactive Archive Shares Secrets of Shell’s Early Climate Research
content:
Campaigners backing attempts to sue Shell over a typhoon in the Philippines have launched an online archive showing that the British oil major knew that burning fossil fuels could harm the climate as early as the 1960s.

ExposeShell.com features documents including a 1966 memo Shell commissioned from British scientist James Lovelock and the ‘Greenhouse Effect’, a confidential 1988 report predicting that human-caused warming could trigger “dramatic” changes in sea level, ocean currents, weather and precipitation — “larger than any that have occurred over the last 12,000 years.” [Read these and other documents in the DeSmog series #ShellKnew]

The interactive site went live as Shell announced the latest figures showing that oil majors are enjoying bumper profits as the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran pushes oil prices higher. Shell said its adjusted third-quarter earnings had doubled to £10.8 billion in comparison to the same period last year.

“We don’t need any more reports to us that this big oily industry has been creating disaster,” Robin Wells, director of Fossil Free London, one of the groups behind the website, said in a statement. “Shell researched the reality but tore up the truth and locked it in the dark.
